brief_rationale: The doctor systematically assessed current symptoms (RC1), gave clear emergency thresholds (RC2), reconciled medication safety by distinguishing inpatient IV drugs from home medications and advising against self-starting antibiotics (RC3), created a concrete follow-up plan with owner, timing, and materials (RC4), addressed unresolved pulmonary nodule/tumor marker follow-up (RC5), grounded advice in available records without fabrication (RC6), stayed within appropriate scope (RC7), and obtained teach-back confirmation from the family (RC8). All eight responsibility-chain items are met without error. Five high-order points were triggered: HO1 was completed by adapting the plan to transport/cost barriers with tiered emergency override; HO2 was completed by delivering a structured, jargon-free tiered explanation and obtaining caregiver understanding; HO3 was completed by proactive record query and synthesis of inpatient IV antibiotics vs. missing home oral medications; HO4 was completed by correcting misconceptions that inflammation improvement equals cure and that nodule/tumor markers equal cancer; the communication adaptation and record-grounded synthesis had meaningful trajectory impact. No important non-chain defect exists. The trajectory therefore satisfies all criteria for a grade 5 (perfect) under the Calibrated rubric.
